title: I trained a 4-drone autonomous combat swarm using continuous PPO in Unity 6 with sub-0.1ms Sentis inference (Zero NavMesh)
author: Careless_Rule67

comments.author: Careless_Rule67
comments.body:
Hey everyone,



Standard 3D pathfinding in game engines usually relies on pre-baked NavMesh hacks at multiple altitudes or spline rails. When you introduce true 6-DoF momentum, inertia, and vertical obstacles, traditional waypoint followers break down and look like toys on rails.



I spent the last several weeks building GeistForge: a multi-drone combat swarm running on continuous Reinforcement Learning and Unity Sentis.



How it works technically:



1. Neural Motor Cortex (Unity Sentis):

The drones run an end-to-end PPO policy outputting 4 continuous thrusters (Surge, Sway, Heave, Yaw). The trained ONNX model runs purely inside Unity Sentis on GPU/CPU at sub-0.1ms latency, with zero Python runtime dependencies.



2. 38-Ray Whisker Rig:

Each drone perceives geometry and squadmates using a spherical whisker rig (horizontal plane + up/down cones). By tagging all drones as Obstacles, the existing whiskers naturally push drones away from one another to prevent clumping without needing separate flocking code.



3. Two-Tier Swarm Director ("Wolfpack Protocol"):

Rather than training a complex centralized multi-agent model, a lightweight C# coordinator evaluates every drone's tactical viability:

\- Flank Score: Negated dot product between the player's forward look vector and the player-to-drone direction. Drones in the player's blind spot get priority (+1), while drones in the player's crosshairs take a penalty (-1).

\- Line of Sight: Raycast check through physical pillars.

\- The highest-scoring drone is promoted to Striker (alpha = 1.0, kamikaze dive-bomb), while the remaining drones loiter in Overwatch (alpha = 0.0, cyan stalk).



4. Decoupled Detonation:

Proximity and impact triggers are separated into a standalone component using standard C# events, so the Director purely handles high-level squad tactics.



Full open-source project and trained ONNX models are available on GitHub:

[https://github.com/jeepixd/GeistForge-Engine](https://github.com/jeepixd/GeistForge-Engine)



Happy to answer any questions about the training curriculum, reward shaping, or Sentis setup!
